The elevator lobby on the second floor of the Main Building is near the student support administration office.
The elevator lobby on the third floor of the Main Building is near the corridor toward the Central Library.
The names of the department offices on the fourth floor of the Main Building are displayed on the floor directory.
A shared printing station available to students is on the fourth floor of the Main Building.
The research labs on the fifth floor of the Main Building are not spaces open to the general public.
The collaborative research lab on the sixth floor of the Main Building is used by authorized research members.
Consultations with the research support office on the seventh floor of the Main Building follow the posted appointment process.
Visitors to staff offices on the eighth floor of the Main Building expect the staff member with whom they have an appointment to be in the office at the scheduled time.
Public administrative services on the ninth floor of the Main Building are provided during each department's operating hours.
The elevators in the Main Building connect the underground parking level through the tenth floor.
The floor directory agent can describe the floors and space names of published facilities.
The floor directory agent cannot check the current occupancy status of meeting rooms.
First-time visitors are more familiar with department names than floor numbers and can more easily understand directions centered on department names.
On public holidays, some administrative offices may not operate even when the Main Building is open.
The floor directory agent cannot verify in real time, at the time of an inquiry, whether published floor-by-floor information matches the actual layout.
Modify campus-wiki/building-access: During the construction period, the third-floor rear entrance cannot be used for general passage.
Modify campus-wiki/building-access: During the construction period, the end time for general access through the main entrance is shortened from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.
Modify campus-wiki/building-access: During the construction period, the existing accessible route cannot be used because it is being reconstructed.
Add campus-wiki/building-access: The temporary accessible route next to the main entrance can be used throughout the construction period.
Modify campus-wiki/building-access: Instruct students authorized to enter after 5:00 p.m. to use a physical NFC student ID card rather than the app.

Modify campus-wiki/building-access: During the construction period, instruct staff and construction/facilities personnel to use only the designated staff entrance instead of the third-floor rear entrance.

Modify campus-wiki/building-access: In access guidance during the construction period, the access guidance agent may prioritize the 5:00 p.m. closing of the main entrance and the closure of the third-floor rear entrance.

Modify campus-wiki/building-access: A student accustomed to reaching the Central Library through the third-floor rear entrance may expect to be able to pass through during the construction period, go as far as the closed rear entrance, and then turn back or search again for an alternative route there.

Add campus-wiki/building-access: During the construction period, the general accessible route bypasses the existing accessible route under reconstruction and leads from the temporary passage next to the main entrance to the first-floor lobby.

Add campus-wiki/building-access: Proactively inform students who are trying to reach the Central Library or who normally use the third-floor rear entrance that they cannot use that route during the construction period.

Modify campus-wiki/building-access: A leader of an external group tour may expect the route used on a previous visit to remain valid during the construction period and lead the visiting group to the closed third-floor rear entrance.

analysis.overview: The frames complement rather than contradict one another: the reference supplies a broad floor directory, navigation context, service expectations, and information limits, while the compared frame adds construction-specific access restrictions, temporary routes, credentials, and proactive warnings. Shared areas preserve their differing operational conditions.
